31	def cluster_by_llm(
32	    labels: list[str],
33	    max_issues: int,
34	    model: str,
35	    token_counter: _TokenCounter | None = None,
36	) -> list[list[int]]:
37	    """
38	    Use an LLM to group failure labels by execution path and symptom.
39	
40	    Each label has the format ``[execution_path] symptom``, where the
41	    execution path shows which sub-agents/tools were called. The LLM
42	    groups labels that share similar execution paths AND similar failure
43	    symptoms into coherent issue categories.
44	
45	    Args:
46	        labels: Failure labels to cluster.
47	        max_issues: Maximum number of groups to produce.
48	        model: Model URI for the clustering LLM.
49	        token_counter: Optional token counter for tracking LLM usage.
50	
51	    Returns:
52	        List of index lists, where each inner list is a cluster of label indices.
53	    """
54	    numbered = "\n".join(f"[{i}] {lbl}" for i, lbl in enumerate(labels))
55	    prompt = CLUSTER_LABELS_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(
56	        num_labels=len(labels),
57	        max_issues=max_issues,
58	        numbered_labels=numbered,
59	    )
60	
61	    response = _call_llm(
62	        model,
63	        [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
64	        response_format=_ClusterResponse,
65	        token_counter=token_counter,
66	    )
67	    content = (response.choices[0].message.content or "").strip()
68	    if not content:
69	        _logger.debug(
70	            "LLM returned empty content for label grouping "
71	            "(finish_reason=%s), falling back to singletons",
72	            response.choices[0].finish_reason,
73	        )
74	        return [[i] for i in range(len(labels))]
75	    result = _ClusterResponse(**json.loads(content))
76	
77	    # Validate indices and collect groups; orphaned indices become singletons
78	    clustered_indices: set[int] = set()
79	    cluster_groups: list[list[int]] = []
80	    for group in result.groups:
81	        if indices := [i for i in group.indices if 0 <= i < len(labels)]:
82	            cluster_groups.append(indices)
83	            clustered_indices.update(indices)
84	
85	    cluster_groups.extend([i] for i in range(len(labels)) if i not in clustered_indices)
86	
87	    # Enforce max_issues limit by keeping the largest groups
88	    if len(cluster_groups) > max_issues:
89	        cluster_groups.sort(key=len, reverse=True)
90	        cluster_groups = cluster_groups[:max_issues]
91	
92	    return cluster_groups

95	def summarize_cluster(
96	    cluster_label_indices: list[int],
97	    analyses: list[_ConversationAnalysis],
98	    model: str,
99	    label_to_analysis: list[int] | None = None,
100	    token_counter: _TokenCounter | None = None,
101	) -> _IdentifiedIssue:
102	    """
103	    Summarize a cluster of analyses into a single identified issue.
104	
105	    Uses an LLM to synthesize a name, description, root cause, and severity
106	    for the cluster. Always returns all corresponding analysis indices as
107	    example_indices (overriding the LLM's selection).
108	
109	    Args:
110	        cluster_label_indices: Label indices that form this cluster.
111	        analyses: All conversation analyses from the pipeline.
112	        model: Model URI for the summarization LLM.
113	        label_to_analysis: Mapping from label index to analysis index.
114	            When ``None``, label indices are used as analysis indices directly.
115	        token_counter: Optional token counter for tracking LLM usage.
116	
117	    Returns:
118	        An ``_IdentifiedIssue`` with synthesized fields and analysis indices.
119	    """
120	    # Map label indices to unique analysis indices (preserving order)
121	    if label_to_analysis is not None:
122	        analysis_indices = list(dict.fromkeys(label_to_analysis[i] for i in cluster_label_indices))
123	    else:
124	        analysis_indices = cluster_label_indices
125	
126	    cluster_analyses = [analyses[i] for i in analysis_indices]
127	    parts = []
128	    for i, analysis in zip(analysis_indices, cluster_analyses):
129	        entry = f"[{i}] {analysis.rationale_summary}"
130	        if analysis.execution_path:
131	            entry += f"\n  execution_path: {analysis.execution_path}"
132	        parts.append(entry)
133	    analyses_text = "\n\n".join(parts)
134	
135	    response = _call_llm(
136	        model,
137	        [
138	            {"role": "system", "content": CLUSTER_SUMMARY_SYSTEM_PROMPT},
139	            {
140	                "role": "user",
141	                "content": f"Cluster of {len(analysis_indices)} analyses:\n\n{analyses_text}",
142	            },
143	        ],
144	        response_format=_IdentifiedIssue,
145	        token_counter=token_counter,
146	    )
147	
148	    content = (response.choices[0].message.content or "").strip()
149	    result = _IdentifiedIssue(**json.loads(content))
150	    result.example_indices = analysis_indices
151	    return result

155	    singletons: list[_IdentifiedIssue],
156	    analysis_labels: dict[int, str],
157	    analyses: list[_ConversationAnalysis],
158	    model: str,
159	    max_issues: int,
160	    token_counter: _TokenCounter | None = None,
161	) -> list[_IdentifiedIssue]:
162	    """
163	    Re-cluster singleton issues via a second LLM pass to find better groupings.
164	
165	    Args:
166	        singletons: Single-analysis issues to attempt merging.
167	        analysis_labels: Mapping from analysis index to its first label string.
168	        analyses: All conversation analyses from the pipeline.
169	        model: Model URI for clustering and summarization.
170	        max_issues: Maximum number of groups to produce.
171	        token_counter: Optional token counter for tracking LLM usage.
172	
173	    Returns:
174	        List of issues after re-clustering (merged or original singletons).
175	    """
176	    if len(singletons) < 2:
177	        return list(singletons)
178	
179	    singleton_labels = []
180	    for singleton in singletons:
181	        idx = singleton.example_indices[0]
182	        singleton_labels.append(analysis_labels.get(idx, singleton.name))
183	
184	    new_groups = cluster_by_llm(singleton_labels, max_issues, model, token_counter=token_counter)
185	
186	    result: list[_IdentifiedIssue] = []
187	    for group in new_groups:
188	        if len(group) == 1:
189	            result.append(singletons[group[0]])
190	            continue
191	        # Each singleton has exactly one analysis index in example_indices
192	        merged_indices = [singletons[group_idx].example_indices[0] for group_idx in group]
193	        merged_issue = summarize_cluster(
194	            merged_indices, analyses, model, token_counter=token_counter
195	        )
196	        if merged_issue.severity >= IssueSeverity.LOW:
197	            result.append(merged_issue)
198	        else:
199	            result.extend(singletons[group_idx] for group_idx in group)
200	
201	    return result
